style: set the scene in one or two plain sentences

candidates.angle: Ananyamanasah means minds fixed on nothing else
candidates.evidence: अनन्यमनसः (with minds fixed on nothing else)

candidates.angle: The great-souled take refuge in divine nature
candidates.evidence: दैवीं प्रकृतिम् आश्रिताः (relying on the divine nature)

candidates.angle: Knowing him as the unborn source of all beings
candidates.evidence: भूत-आदिम् अव्ययम् (the source of beings, imperishable)

angle_en: Ananyamanasah: minds fixed on nothing else
angle_hi: अनन्यमनसः: ऐसे मन जो किसी और चीज़ में न लगे हों

en.intro: Krishna contrasts the deluded with the great-minded. Listen for the kind of mind that can truly see him.
en.notice: Ananyamanasah means minds fixed on nothing else. The great-minded do not scatter their attention; they hold it on Krishna alone and worship him as the imperishable source of all beings.
en.next: Krishna then describes how these steadfast souls worship him through chanting, striving, and bowing.
en.meaning: But, Arjuna, the great-minded ones, relying on the divine nature, worship Me with one-pointed minds, knowing Me as the unborn and imperishable source of all beings.

hi.intro: कृष्ण भ्रमित लोगों के विपरीत महात्मनों की बात करते हैं। सुनिए कि वह किस तरह के मन की बात कर रहे हैं।
hi.meaning: परन्तु हे पार्थ, महात्मन, जो दैवी प्रकृति को आश्रय देते हैं, वे अनन्य मन से मुझे सम्पूर्ण प्राणियों का आदि और अव्यय जानकर मेरा भजन करते हैं।
hi.notice: अनन्यमनसः का अर्थ है ऐसे मन जो किसी और चीज़ में न लगे हों। ये महात्मन अपना ध्यान केवल कृष्ण पर केंद्रित रखते हैं और उन्हें सभी प्राणियों का अविनाशी स्रोत मानकर उनकी पूजा करते हैं।
hi.next: कृष्ण बताते हैं कि ये दृढ़ लोग किस प्रकार जप, तप और भक्ति से उनकी पूजा करते हैं।

en.intro: Krishna contrasts the deluded with the great-minded. Listen for the kind of mind that can truly see him.
en.body: But, Arjuna, the great-minded ones, relying on the divine nature, worship Me with one-pointed minds, knowing Me as the unborn and imperishable source of all beings. Ananyamanasah means minds fixed on nothing else. The great-minded do not scatter their attention; they hold it on Krishna alone and worship him as the imperishable source of all beings. Krishna then describes how these steadfast souls worship him through chanting, striving, and bowing.
